decisions.statement: Every workstation service is put up at once rather than one service at a time.
The code a unit runs is spelled under the tree the deploy pinned rather than under the checkout.
The pages a unit reads and writes are read under the main checkout rather than under that tree.
A unit akasha owns that no service accounts for is taken away by this call.
A home directory nothing states refuses the call.
The loader and one manifest for each service are written where the units are.
A manifest carries the closure the deploy read for that service.
The port the loader reaches is the one the pages service's own page states.
A dry run reports the plan the run would carry out and writes nothing.
A systemctl that refuses makes the call refuse.
A service is restarted where a file its own closure holds changed since the last deploy.
A scheduled service is restarted by nothing, since its next tick reads the tree as the tree is.
Nothing here reads the command line.

definition: every workstation service's units written from one pinned tree and asked of systemd
